top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B010) rewards a distinct, identifiable discovery: firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting and foreign investment, with reallocation across firms as a channel for gains from trade. It yields predictions that representative-firm trade theory does not and that firm-level data have tested for over twenty years. Credit follows the intellectual structure (Melitz 2003; Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple) under the three-name cap. The costs are real: precursors such as Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn go uncredited, welfare magnitudes depend on distributional assumptions, and the 2008 trade prize raises a distinctness question. A narrow citation on the mechanism and a scientific background acknowledging precursors can address these. No award is clearly worse than a well-founded, mature discovery, so P000 ranks last. My judgment rests on recollection of the literature and is not independently verified.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to Helpman or Melitz. Disclosed only: SSE affiliation alongside committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and my research field (matching and market design) is not the field of the proposal.
